title: Quantum percolation conjecture on regular trees
abstract: For Bernoulli bond percolation on every regular tree of degree at least three, we prove that infinite clusters appear strictly before absolutely continuous spectrum. Throughout an explicit supercritical interval, the adjacency operator of every open cluster almost surely has no absolutely continuous component. Together with Bordenave's theorem, this gives $p_c<p_{ac}<1$.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes quantum percolation on regular trees, proving that the threshold for infinite cluster formation ($p_c$) is strictly lower than the threshold for the appearance of an absolutely continuous spectrum ($p_{ac}$). The methodology combines advanced spectral theory, resolvent analysis, and contraction mapping arguments to establish this crucial separation in the system's spectral properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the relationship between the onset of infinite connected components (percolation) and the appearance of extended quantum states (absolutely continuous spectrum) in random subgraphs of regular trees.
main_result: The authors prove a strict separation between the percolation threshold ($p_c$) and the threshold for the appearance of an absolutely continuous spectrum ($p_{ac}$), showing $p_c < p_{ac}$ for regular trees.
method: The analysis heavily relies on spectral theory, specifically examining the boundary values of the resolvent operator using fixed-point equations and contraction mapping principles.
model_or_system: The system is Bernoulli bond percolation on a regular tree of degree $k+1 \ge 3$. The quantum dynamics are governed by the adjacency operator $A_\omega$ acting on the graph's Hilbert space.
key_observables: Connectivity threshold ($p_c$), onset of absolutely continuous spectrum ($p_{ac}$), and the spectral measure $\mu_u(B)$ derived from the resolvent's imaginary part.
important_parameters: The degree of the tree ($k+1$), the bond retention probability ($p$), and the critical probability $p_c = 1/k$.
main_assumptions: The proof requires establishing that the imaginary part of the resolvent boundary value is zero almost surely, which is achieved via contraction estimates on probability measures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the separation of regimes: $p_c = 1/k$ to $1/k + \epsilon_k$ (where no a.c. spectrum exists) and the region governed by Bordenave's theorem.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first defining the spectral diagnostics, then using recursive relations for the resolvent ($\Gamma_T(z)$), establishing contraction bounds ($ho_k < 1$), and finally proving that the imaginary part of the resolvent is zero almost surely, leading to the spectral conclusion.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding spectral localization in disordered quantum systems, directly addressing the quantum percolation conjecture in a highly structured setting (trees).
